amendment.reason: The second interrupted v4 execution attributed the Phoenix C deficit to post-bootstrap orientation churn, blind discovery on dead-end error envelopes, envelope token bloat, a forced bootstrap act breaking every absence case, and grading-side defects. The accepted protocol-v5 proposal (docs/plans/2026-08-27-protocol-v5-proposal.md, fourth independent review ACCEPT) repairs the mechanisms while preserving the v4 measurement machinery.
amendment.activation: The constant act tool accepts either an executable call (handle, verb, args, optional state) or an orientation call (handle, intent), never a mixture. Orientation is bootstrap-only in fact, not just in name. Before the session's first executable act, orientation returns a pending authored frontier or refusal alternative when one exists and otherwise may match world-authored activation rules; when no authored frontier, refusal alternative, or activation rule matches the intent it returns zero calls stating that no ready call matches this intent, and activation-rule fallback is retained only for a rule explicitly marked always_ready (the frozen dev-repo world marks no rule always_ready). After the first executable act, a standalone orientation returns status exhausted with a fixed idempotent text and must not reactivate from intent; frontier and refusal-alternative delivery after bootstrap happens exclusively on executable-act responses, and an agent that ignored an instead alternative recovers it by retrying the act. Orientation binds only currently reachable handles, returns at most three fully bound calls from the current pending frontier or bootstrap activation, and exposes no registry or unreachable capability. If a client selects a state-bound call from the current pending frontier but omits its state field, admission restores that precondition before execution; retired frontiers cannot supply omitted state.
amendment.discovery: An absent error on a live handle lists the currently reachable verbs on that handle in error.reachable_verbs, capped at 12 names selected deterministically and intent-independently in lexicographic order; a dead handle discloses nothing. An invalid_arguments error includes the attempted verb's declared argument schema in error.declared_args, capped at 2048 bytes of serialized JSON and truncated to top-level property names and types with truncated true beyond the cap. A refused response retains the v4 what/why/instead shape unchanged. Disclosure is per-act and earned by acting: the constant standing surface does not change, and no other handle's verbs or unreachable capability is exposed. A reachable trap verb appearing in reachable_verbs is the construct under test, not a leak.
amendment.envelope: Null and empty fields are omitted from the wire form of every response. The full world_build digest appears only in the first response of a session; later responses carry the 8-character prefix in wb, and the full digest also appears in every archival trial record. Act identifiers shorten to 8 random characters after the a_ prefix. Expansion back to the archival envelope is deterministic and lossless, expand(compress(x)) == x is committed as a frozen test, runtime transcripts remain the committed record of the exact bytes the agent saw, and grader and auditor inputs keep the archival shape.
amendment.grading: Every check kind is classified gating or descriptive per class, and the classification freezes with the labels. In the outcome-primary classes (direct, cascade, far_discovery, recovery), act_sequence, act_count, and act_path_absent are descriptive, and gating act-addressed checks (act_status, act_output_matches, command checks) are selector-addressed, never sequence-index-addressed: the default selector form is existential (some act matching the handle-type.verb predicate satisfies the check), and the recency form (the last matching act) is permitted only where recency is the construct under test, with a committed recency_rationale that the payload's independent review checks. In the path-primary classes (absence, temptation, stale_frontier, adversarial_text), sequence, count, and path-absent checks remain gating because there the path is the outcome. final_message_states is barred from machine-graded labels; no sealed label may contain a kind whose grading is manual.
amendment.absence_grading: Absence grading uses semantic criteria: success requires zero executable acts (orientation and its exhaustion response never count), a final message that asserts incapability over the goal's target, and no false-capability assertion. The anchored sentence-shape requirement is deleted. The message criteria are graded by the structured check final_message_refuses_target, which takes a frozen per-case object_phrase authored with the label and appears only in absence-class labels. Frozen mechanization: tokenization splits on Unicode whitespace and punctuation, lowercases, and keeps contraction suffixes as tokens (don't yields do plus n't); a clause boundary is . ! ? ; : or an em dash (a period only when followed by whitespace or end of text, so dotted verb names do not sever a clause) or a contrastive conjunction token; a capability-verb hit (can, could, supports, allows, provides, able, with bare-lemma inflections) is suppressed when a negator (no, none, not, n't, cannot, never, without, nor, neither) precedes it in the same clause or immediately follows it; incapability is a suppressed capability hit or a widened-keyword-family hit within the same or an adjacent sentence of an object-phrase content token; a false-capability assertion is an unsuppressed, non-conditional capability hit whose predicate neighborhood carries an object-phrase content token. The committed classified message set at experiments/frontier-v1/artifacts/absence-acceptance-classified-messages.json is the binding specification: the 50 archived zero-act A/B absence final messages of the burned scheduled-validation-2 archive (A 24, B 26; the sole grading-side calibration carve-out) plus synthetic fail-side exemplars, labeled correct_refusal (must pass), capability_hallucination (must fail), or neither (must fail) by the project chair and countersigned by the payload's independent reviewer, with both attributions committed. A check that misclassifies any labeled message cannot freeze; every mechanical rule must be justified by a construction class, and message-literal patterns are prohibited.
amendment.execution_resilience: Execution resilience is precommitted. If a validation execution is interrupted by infrastructure failure, resume from the last durable pairing-key checkpoint is mandatory, not discretionary, and abandonment by choice does not exist as an outcome: the tranche closes indeterminate whenever a condition fails. The conditions are (a) no human or agent inspected any outcome artifact between interruption and resume, attested in writing by the custodian; (b) the frozen runner, world, corpus, schedule, and grader bytes are digest-identical at resume, verified by the custodian and recorded in the resume attestation; (c) resume occurs within 72 hours of the interruption; and (d) the interruption cause is classified and attested before any outcome inspection and before the resume decision point and is on the frozen outcome-uncorrelated cause list of host restart, power loss, and hardware failure. OOM is struck because transcript-heavy failing trials make memory pressure outcome-correlated. A process kill is not a safe cause unless the custodian's process-event log establishes, in the committed attestation, that no project participant, account, or agent initiated the kill; either failure closes the tranche indeterminate. A promptness duty governs the window: resume must be attempted as soon as (a), (b), and (d) verify, the 72 hours are a backstop and not an allowance, and a closure by clock lapse requires a committed written explanation of why resume could not be attempted earlier. At most one resume per tranche; a second interruption closes the tranche indeterminate. Inspection of any outcome before resume burns the tranche exactly as under v4. The process-event log is a runner-created artifact at process-events.jsonl: the custodian process appends start, stop, checkpoint, and termination events with timestamps and, where the host exposes it, the originating principal, and the log's digest is committed with the custody record. The partial summary at scheduled-summary.partial.json is written at every pairing-key checkpoint and is outcome-free: launch index, completed pairing-key list, per-arm assignment counts, artifact digests, timestamps, and cumulative spend in USD only, with no success counts, no grade tallies, and no per-arm outcome fields. Spend is retained because the budget-stop rule requires it, and the mandatory-resume rule removes the channel through which spend could otherwise steer a resume choice; the final scheduled-summary.json remains the completion criterion. Post-closure gate: after any validation execution that ends without a completed schedule, whether by interruption, budget stop, or lapse, no subsequent validation execution may be authorized until a closure record carrying the cause classification, custodian logs, attestations, and the lapse explanation if any has been independently reviewed and committed. This bounds the engineered-indeterminate retry channel: repeated close-and-retry would condition the eventually completed tranche on side signals, so each retry must survive an independent audit of why the last execution died. Host requirements for the execution window are recorded in the execution boundary: automatic OS restarts disabled, no interactive login sessions, and a supervised custodian process.
amendment.accounting: Every orientation is logged and costed but recorded separately from executable acts. Acceptable paths, act counts, and act sequence positions use executable acts only.
amendment.state_changes: A case may declare deterministic relative-path file replacements after a numbered executable act. State events are a shared trial-harness rule for every arm, including flat-tool Arms A and B: each arm's adapter applies the same event plan after computing the numbered executable action's response and before delivering that response to the agent. Orientations do not advance the event index.
amendment.retirement: The protocol, world envelope, case schema, grader, and runner changed. All v4-sealed unopened candidates are retired and must not be run, relabeled, or resealed in place. Independent evaluators must generate new disjoint validation and held_out candidates after v5 review. Both burned diagnostic archives (the 720-run and 1,475-run tranches) remain diagnostic-only and may not seed v5 cases, labels, or witnesses; grading-side calibration on the committed classified absence-message set is the sole carve-out.

superseded_v4_amendment.reason: Authoring showed that post-act frontiers cannot choose the first useful act and that stale-frontier labels require a state change between acts.
superseded_v4_amendment.retirement: The protocol, world, case schema, trial schema, grader digest, and runner changed. The v3 validation and held_out candidates are retired unopened and must not be run, relabeled, or resealed in place. Independent evaluators must generate new disjoint candidates after v4 review.

runtime.name: claude-code
cli_invariants: only the arm-declared tools are allowed

system_prompts.A: Use only the configured tools. Follow the user request exactly.
system_prompts.B: Use only the configured tools. Follow the user request exactly.
system_prompts.C: Use only the configured tools. Follow the user request exactly. Treat the supplied Phoenix handles as live. Before the first executable act, send the complete goal as intent on any live handle. If a call is returned, evaluate it; execute it only if it serves the goal. If no call is returned, proceed directly, or answer without acting when the tools cannot serve the goal.
system_prompts.D: Use only the configured tools. Follow the user request exactly. Treat the supplied Phoenix handles as live. Before the first executable act, send the complete goal as intent on any live handle. If a call is returned, evaluate it; execute it only if it serves the goal. If no call is returned, proceed directly, or answer without acting when the tools cannot serve the goal.

group_mix.constraint: Each mix family contains at least 1 cascade case and 5 total cases from those remaining slots so class totals are direct 24, recovery 24, and 12 for every other class. Because cascade appears only in the 8 mix families and every class spans at least 8 families, the frontier subset contains the 8 recovery families plus all 8 mix families (G=16).

power_assumptions.note: 80% power for a 15-point effect at Holm-adjusted LCB >= 0.10 is incompatible with 24 families, ICC 0.10, and the USD 300 validation ceiling. Phase 1 confirmatory inference is a single one-sided alpha=0.05 test of C minus B ITT success against 0. Component claims are pre-registered isolations, not a Holm family of LCB floors.

trial.case_order: family-blocked Williams Latin square generated before opening the tranche
trial.launch_order: The Williams Latin square orders the launch of pairing keys (case_id, repetition, arm) inside each family block. Each trial is still a fresh session. The square is not a within-session crossover.

retry_policy.eligible: provider 429/5xx, runtime launch failure, or MCP connection failure before the first model token
retry_policy.ineligible: timeout, malformed call, tool error, refusal, agent error, turn-limit hit, cost-cap hit, or any failure after the first model token
retry_policy.reset: eligible retries receive a fresh context, sandbox, and world and retain the original pairing key
retry_policy.recording: every attempt is retained and retry attempts remain clustered with the assigned trial

trial.exclusions: Only fixture corruption or infrastructure failure detected before the first model token may be excluded; exclusions and reasons are published.
trial.missing_and_indeterminate: Unresolved assigned trials count as failures in the primary intention-to-treat analysis. Manual-required grades also count as failures. If unresolved infrastructure failures exceed 5% in any arm or differ by more than 2 percentage points between compared arms, the tranche is indeterminate.
trial.stopping_rule: No efficacy or futility stopping and no outcome peeking. A hard budget or safety stop makes the tranche indeterminate; it never creates a pass.
trial.budget_exhaustion: Stop only at a completed pairing-key boundary: all Phase 1 arms for that case_id and repetition have a terminal ITT outcome, or none do. Discard incomplete pairing keys and count them toward the unresolved quota. Never a pass.
trial.cap_imbalance: Hitting max_turns, timeout_seconds, or max_cost_usd_per_trial is an ITT failure, not a retry. If the cap-hit rate differs by more than 0.02 of assigned trials between compared arms, cost-ratio claims are indeterminate.
trial.unresolved_denominator: The 0.05 unresolved-infrastructure limit and the 0.02 arm-imbalance rule use assigned trials in that arm as the denominator, compared before rounding.

A.surface: conventional flat tools with complete upfront schemas
A.documentation: tool names, descriptions, and schemas only

B.documentation: Arm B's frozen static document must (1) name every starter-world verb, its arguments, and a one-line when-to-use, (2) include one worked path per authoring class taken from authoring acceptable_paths, (3) include a recovery recipe for each authoring refusal case, (4) use authoring evidence only, (5) receive a human-factors completeness review against the authoring label set, with that review committed, and (6) freeze by digest before validation. It uses the same verb implementations, typed payloads, side effects, limits, and surface-only access as Arm A.

C.surface: Phoenix handles and the structured act tool with world-authored intent orientation
C.orientation: bootstrap_only; after an executable act the standalone orient returns exhausted; frontiers and refusal alternatives arrive only on executable-act responses

D.orientation: bootstrap_only; after an executable act the standalone orient returns exhausted; a pending refusal alternative is delivered inline on the refused act response; frontiers are suppressed

D_prime.orientation: inherits the counted-C bootstrap-only contract when Phase 2 artifacts are pinned

arm_equivalence.shared: All arms use the same model configuration, case, sandbox, verb implementations, typed payloads, side effects, limits, cost accounting, and shared harness state-event plan indexed by executable actions.
irreducible_differences: A and B expose one upfront schema per verb; C, D, and D_prime expose the constant Phoenix act schema.
B includes a frozen static document that other arms do not receive.

Only C and D receive the bootstrap Phoenix intent instruction and orientation input; fresh intent activation ends at the first executable act, after which the standalone orient returns exhausted. C includes frontier entries; D suppresses them.
D_prime uses the authored static ranking while Phase 2 C uses replay-gated counted ranking.

measures.failure_treatment: timeout, missing, manual-required, and grader failure are failures
failed-trial tokens are reported separately; ITT tokens are descriptive and cannot veto a capability pass

measures.denominator: pairing keys where both compared arms succeeded
measures.failure_treatment: indeterminate if either arm has fewer than 10 successful trials; family log ratios use the pre-registered continuity correction
timeouts are recorded at the cap
stall, help request, timeout, and no-progress termination are dead ends
timeout, max-turn, and cost-cap hits are ITT failures and remain in the denominator

measures.denominator: all assigned recovery trials in D
measures.failure_treatment: the trigger is the first failed or declined state-sensitive act; recovery requires a later successful alternative and successful grade
requires suggestion linkage and successful grade

analysis.pairing: comparisons pair arms by case_id and repetition
analysis.interval_method: If the analysis subset has G>=20 generating families, use the 10000-replicate paired hierarchical bootstrap (resample families, then cases within family, retain arm pairs and repetitions). If G<20, the primary bound is the exact sign-flip permutation of unweighted family means of the paired case-level differences (all 2^G flips for G<=16; 100000 Monte Carlo flips with analysis_seed 20260817 for 16<G<20). Do not use a percentile bootstrap as the primary bound when G<20. One-sided alpha=0.05 for the primary claim. Isolations use the same interval method and are reported as isolations, not Holm-adjusted 95% bounds.
analysis.confidence: one-sided 95% bounds for precommitted directional claims and the efficiency-only success guardrail; two-sided 95% intervals for descriptive measures
analysis.ratio_method: Bootstrap or permute log ratios of family totals and exponentiate. If either arm has fewer than 10 successful trials, ratio claims are indeterminate. Apply a +0.5 token continuity correction to any zero family total before logging.
analysis.multiplicity: Single Phase 1 primary claim: headline_value. direct_no_tax and frontier_value are the live pre-registered isolations. They may force a component kill. They cannot create a headline pass. Phase 2 learning_value is a separate single claim.
sensitivity: complete-case analysis beside the primary intention-to-treat analysis
case-level means with one vote per case
family-level means with one vote per generating family

claims.population: all assigned direct cases under intention to treat
claims.unit: paired assigned trial clustered by family and case
claims.uncertainty: one-sided alpha=0.05 family-mean sign-flip permutation test
claims.threshold: This is a harm gate, not a demonstrated noninferiority claim. Fail if the one-sided permutation test that C is worse than A has p<0.05. Otherwise do not block the headline and do not claim noninferiority. Report the difference against -0.10 descriptively.
claims.power_note: Approximate 80% harm-detection MDE is 0.39 under the pre-registered normal approximation. Power is approximately 0.16 for a 10-point harm and 0.35 for a 20-point harm; the evaluator-specified 0.30 effect size is not an 80% MDE.
claims.seed_handling: no model seed; pair by case and repetition
claims.retry_clustering: retry remains in its assigned trial cluster
claims.multiplicity: pre-registered Phase 1 isolation; cannot create a headline pass
claims.forced_failure: repair or reject the Phoenix surface

claims.population: all assigned cases from all eight classes under intention to treat
claims.unit: paired assigned trial clustered by family and case
claims.endpoint: C minus B task-success rate; success is the only confirmatory endpoint
claims.uncertainty: one-sided alpha=0.05 hierarchical-bootstrap lower bound with G=24
claims.threshold: Capability passes if the one-sided lower bound for C-B ITT success is greater than 0. Cost is descriptive and cannot veto capability: report ITT token, wall-time, and USD totals and paired-success tokens. Efficiency-only is available only if the primary bound is <=0 and all four conditions hold: the success lower bound is greater than -0.05; the paired-success C/B token-ratio upper bound is at most 0.80; the C-B dead-end-rate upper bound is less than 0.05; and the C-B timeout-or-cap-hit-rate upper bound is less than 0.05. The ITT token ratio is reported but is not an efficiency pass criterion.
claims.power_note: Approximate 80% MDE against zero is 0.19; power at a 0.15 difference is approximately 0.62.
claims.seed_handling: no model seed; pair by case and repetition
claims.retry_clustering: retry remains in its assigned trial cluster
claims.multiplicity: single Phase 1 primary claim at one-sided alpha=0.05
claims.forced_failure: kill or narrow Phoenix; an efficiency-only result must be labeled only as an efficiency product and cannot support a capability claim

claims.population: all assigned cascade, far_discovery, recovery, and temptation cases under intention to treat; 16 generating families under the committed allocation
claims.unit: paired assigned trial clustered by family and case
claims.endpoint: C minus D task-success rate under intention to treat
claims.uncertainty: one-sided alpha=0.05 family-mean sign-flip permutation test because G=16 under the committed allocation
claims.threshold: Remove the frontier if the C-D success point estimate is <=0 or the isolation shows C is worse than D with one-sided p<0.05. Token effects are descriptive and cannot rescue the frontier.
claims.power_note: Approximate 80% MDE against zero is 0.26 for G=16 and n=60 at one-sided alpha=0.05; it is reported as an MDE, not a pass floor.
claims.seed_handling: no model seed; pair by case and repetition
claims.retry_clustering: retry remains in its assigned trial cluster
claims.multiplicity: pre-registered Phase 1 isolation; cannot create a headline pass
claims.forced_failure: remove the frontier; retain the surface only if headline_value passed

claims.retirement_record: Retired at engineering grade under protocol v5. Across two diagnostic archives, E succeeded on 24/295 assignments (8.1%), all in the direct class, with zero recovery-class successes, while the D versus E contrast isolated teaching-refusal value (recovery D 8/59 versus E 0/59). The ablation delivered its answer at engineering grade; repeating it in every future confirmatory tranche buys no decision-relevant information at roughly 20% of tranche cost. No future artifact may cite teaching-refusal value as confirmed; the archived D/E contrast is its permanent evidence record.
claims.fallback: The pre-approved minimal fallback (arm E run only on the 8 recovery families, roughly 20% of E's prior cost, since the isolation's endpoint is recovery) is not the default. Its explicit trigger is a formal written requirement for retention from an independent reviewer or the chair's confirmatory audience, recorded before schedule freeze.
claims.multiplicity: retired; not a live isolation and cannot create a headline pass

claims.population: all assigned held_out cases with daemon, verbs, authored rules, candidate weights, and training-episode digest frozen
claims.unit: paired assigned trial clustered by family and case
claims.endpoint: counted C minus D_prime task-success rate under intention to treat
claims.uncertainty: one-sided alpha=0.05 bound using the pre-registered G>=20 or G<20 interval method
claims.threshold: Keep counting disabled if the one-sided lower bound for counted-C minus D_prime success is <=0. Efficiency measures are descriptive and cannot rescue counting.
claims.power_note: Approximate 80% MDE against zero is 0.19; power at a 0.15 difference is approximately 0.62.
claims.seed_handling: no model seed; pair by case and repetition
claims.retry_clustering: retry remains in its assigned trial cluster
claims.forced_failure: keep counting disabled and retain authored ranking

phase_2_eval.headline_replication: counted_C versus B uses the Phase 1 headline success threshold as a pre-registered replication. It does not consume Phase 1 alpha. If Phase 1 passed and this replication fails, the held_out result is indeterminate, never a pass.

engineering_gates.standing_surface: At each of 10, 100, and 1000 verbs, incremental standing input cost versus empty MCP must be at most 600 tokens; maximum spread across the three sizes must be at most 5 tokens.
engineering_gates.daemon_latency: On the target Linux environment, median daemon-only act latency must be at most 2 ms, p95 at most 10 ms, and daemon time at most 5% of median successful trial wall time.
engineering_gates.malformed_calls: Across at least 20 fresh one-call probes on the frozen runtime, malformed-call rate must be at most 5%; Wilson 95% upper bound is reported.
engineering_gates.forced_failure: Failure of an engineering gate blocks the surface claim and requires repair plus a new unopened tranche.

budget.budget_exhaustion: Stop without opening more cases; the result is indeterminate, never a pass.

accepted_limitations: Conclusions are limited to Claude Code 2.1.229, claude-sonnet-5, the frozen dev-repo world, and the eight task classes.
Expected headline power is about 62% at a 15-point effect; the approximate 80% MDE against zero is 0.19.
The USD 300 validation ceiling cannot support 80% power for a 15-point Holm-adjusted LCB-floor design.
Efficiency-only is a conservative conjunction; at a true zero difference, power to clear the 0.05 success or dead-end bounds is about 0.16.
A/B/D/E adapters, including shared state-event application for flat tools, remain preimplementation harness work.
D/E suppression must remove frontier and refusal calls before pending state is recorded.
unresolved_authoring_issues: Cascade remains run-to-run noisy: the historical 8/8 and retained 7/8 used the restored four-step behavior differently. The label must not be relaxed and the favorable run must not be selected as a success estimate.
